title: He said that…
goal: Report what someone said, moving the tense back
intro: When we report what someone said, the tense usually moves one step back: “I am tired” → She said she was tired. Pronouns and time words change too: “tomorrow” becomes “the next day”. Use “say” without a person, and “tell” with a person: He said that… / He told me that….

rules.rule: Tense moves back: am → was, will → would, can → could, went → had gone.
examples: “I’m busy.” → He said he was busy.
“I’ll call.” → She said she would call.
She said that she was leaving.
She told me that she was leaving.

rules.rule: If it’s still true, you can keep the tense.
examples: He said he lives in Pune.
She said the shop opens at ten.

mistakes.wrong: He said me that he was busy.
mistakes.right: He told me that he was busy.

mistakes.wrong: She told that she will come.
mistakes.right: She said that she would come.

mistakes.wrong: He said that he is coming tomorrow. (said last week)
mistakes.right: He said that he was coming the next day.
mistakes.why: Move the tense and the time back.

mistakes.wrong: I told to him the truth.

ex.q: He ___ that he would be late.
“I can help.” → She said she ___ help.
My friend said me that the exam was easy.
ex.fixed: My friend told me that the exam was easy.

ex.q: She told that she liked the gift.
ex.fixed: She said that she liked the gift.

ex.q: He said he will send it soon.
ex.fixed: He said he would send it soon.

ex.q: “I don’t know.” → He said he ___ know.

ex.a: She told me that she was moving to Canada.

ex.q: Report it: Rahul said, “I am hungry.”
a: Rahul said that he was hungry

talk: Report a recent conversation you had with someone: what they said, what they told you, and what you said back.
